land.text: Egypt, 'effectively taking control of the country' after al-Adid's death in 1171

predecessors.note: The Ayyubid page gives 1171 as the founding year; Cliopatria's Ayyubid row only begins in 1177 (the Fatimid row runs to 1176).

land.text: Damascus (from 23 November 1174), Hama and Homs (1175), Aleppo (1182) and the Jazira cities (1182-83), taken piecemeal from Nur al-Din's Zengid heirs

predecessors.note: Not a birth handover: the Zengid lands came to the Ayyubids over 1174-1183 (ledger).

land.text: Egypt from April 1250 (the Bahri Mamluks); Damascus and southern Syria after Ain Jalut (September 1260); Homs 1262, Kerak c. 1263, Hama 1341 (Mamluk dossier)

successors.note: Ayyubid rule in Egypt ended in 1250; the Syrian rump ended with the Mongol conquest of 1260.

land.text: Aleppo, sacked by the Mongols in 1260, 'and the Ayyubids' remaining territories soon after'

successors.note: The Mongols held northern Syria only briefly in 1260 (Mamluk dossier).

capitals.name: Damascus
capitals.note: Infobox: Damascus (1174-1218); Saladin was welcomed there on 23 November 1174.

capitals.name: Aleppo
capitals.note: Infobox: Aleppo (1250-1260), the seat of an-Nasir Yusuf's Syrian rump after Egypt was lost.

correction.text: Egypt after the end of the Fatimid caliphate, 1171-1173

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Ayyubid row begins in 1177, but the page's infobox gives 'Established by Saladin: 1171' and 'In 1171, al-Adid died and Saladin ... effectively taking control of the country'. Egypt alone until Damascus (November 1174) and Yemen (May 1174). Ibrim in Lower Nubia was raided in 1173 (Saladin page) and is not drawn.

minus.text: Egypt, Damascus and its Syrian hinterland, Yemen and the Hejaz; Aleppo was still Zengid

union.text: the Yemeni interior and Hadramawt, taken in 1175 (Sanaa) and 1180 (Hadramawt)
Arabia outside the Hejaz (Asir, Najran and Jizan to the south, Al Jawf to the north), which the page does not give to the Ayyubids
Transjordan, the Frankish lordship of Kerak until 1187

minus.text: land not yet Ayyubid at the end of 1174

union.text: Cliopatria's 1177 Ayyubid shape without Aleppo and without what was taken later
all Egypt, as drawn since the founding in 1171

correction.text: Egypt, Cyrenaica, Damascus and its hinterland, the Yemeni coast (Zabid, Aden) and the Hejaz, at the end of 1174; Aleppo still Zengid

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1174-1176: Egypt, Damascus (Saladin welcomed there on 23 November 1174) and Yemen (Zabid May 1174, Aden later in 1174, Sanaa 1175), i.e. Cliopatria's 1177 shape without Aleppo. Hama and Homs fell only in 1175 (Saladin page), so 1174 is drawn slightly too large; the Hejaz is in the 1173 commission to Turan-Shah but no year is given for it. fx-27: narrowed to the ledger's end of 1174 (the Yemeni interior, Arabia outside the Hejaz (Asir, Najran and Jizan; Al Jawf in the north), Hama and Homs, and Transjordan cut: the page has Hama and Homs 'by 1175', Sanaa 1175, Hadramawt 1180, Karak and Mont Real 'soon fell' in 1187 and the Ayyubid page gives no year for the Hejaz); Egypt entire added so the 1171 founding country is not trimmed by the Cliopatria shape; Cyrenaica comes from the new 1173 gain.

correction.text: 1177-1181: the Ayyubid realm without Aleppo (Aleppo formally entered Ayyubid hands on 12 June of the year it was taken)

keyframe_review.note: 2.0 M km2 'est. 1190 (high-end estimate of peak area)' against this shape's 1.72 M km2 (ratio 0.86; the 1190 figure belongs to the later, larger shape). The shape holds Aleppo only in part: 'In May 1182, Saladin captured Aleppo' (Ayyubid page; the Saladin page: 'By 1182, Saladin had completed the conquest of Syria after capturing Aleppo'), so for 1177-1181 Aleppo comes out. The 1182 changes are the next new keyframe.

correction.text: 1182-1187: Egypt, Syria with Aleppo, the Jazira and Yemen, before the conquest of Jerusalem on 2 October 1187

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1182-1187: Aleppo (1182), the Jazira (Edessa, Saruj, Raqqa, Qirqesiya, Nusaybin, Sinjar on 30 December) and Amid (the Saladin page places it in 1183) come in, but not yet the Crusader lands. Drawn as Cliopatria's 1188 shape minus the Kingdom of Jerusalem's 1186 shape. The Saladin page says Raqqa, Sinjar and Nusaybin were given back to Imad al-Din Zangi II as Ayyubid vassals (see the Ayyubid page).

1.83 M km2 against the page's 2.0 M km2 at 1190 (ratio 0.92). Adds Palestine after Hattin (4 July 1187) and Jerusalem ('capitulated to his forces on Friday, 2 October 1187', Saladin page); the shape begins a year after the conquest.

correction.text: unchanged shape; the Zengid lands of Mosul (Cliopatria's Zengid 1188 shape) are to be drawn in the vassal tint, not as direct Ayyubid land: 'left the Zengids in control of Mosul'

keyframe_review.note: 2.03 M km2 against the page's 2.0 M km2 at 1190 (ratio 1.02). The shape swallows 778 of the 797 cells of Cliopatria's Zengid 1188 shape (Mosul and the Zengid Jazira) and adds Amid. The page says the March 1186 treaty 'left the Zengids in control of Mosul' while they ceded the land east of the Lesser Zab and promised military aid: that is a vassal, not direct land. The coast from Tyre to Jaffa leaves the shape at the Treaty of Ramla (1/2 September 1192).

1.82 M km2 against the page's 1.7 M km2 low-end estimate for 1200 (ratio 1.07). 'With their support, al-Adil conquered Cairo in 1200' and 'entered [Damascus] in triumph in 1201': the realm is reunited under al-Adil. Cliopatria's Zengid row reappears in 1202, consistent with Mosul being outside the direct shape.
unverified: page budget. Same area as 1202 (1.82 M km2); the pages opened give no territorial change for 1220 (the Fifth Crusade's Damietta campaign was not read).

correction.text: from 1229: without Jerusalem and its coast corridor, Bethlehem, Nazareth, Jaffa and Toron, and without Yemen

keyframe_review.note: Two changes the shape misses, both from 1229: 'al-Kamil surrendered Jerusalem with the exception of some Muslim holy sites' and 'Frederick also received Bethlehem and Nazareth, part of Sidon district, and Jaffa and Toron' with 'a narrow corridor to the coast' (treaty of 18 February 1229, a ten-year truce); and Yemen, which Nur ad-Din Umar declared independent after Mas'ud's death in 1229 (Ayyubid page; the Rasulid page's text says 1235). 1227-1228 stand as drawn.

correction.text: 1236-1243: without the Frankish Jerusalem, Bethlehem, Nazareth and Jaffa

keyframe_review.note: Yemen is already out of this shape (matching the Rasulid page's infobox 1229 or text 1235), but Jerusalem and the corridor are still drawn: the Franks kept them 'for over ten years' (Ayyubid page) until al-Salih Ayyub 'gained possession of Jerusalem' in 1244-45. The Ayyubid page says the Rasulids completed the end of Ayyubid suzerainty in the Hejaz in 1238 'when Nur al-Din Umar captured Mecca'; the Rasulid page calls the hold 'temporary' and no page dates the return, so the Hejaz stays in the shape (a gap, see the ledger).

minus.text: Cliopatria's Ayyubid and mislabelled 'Mamluk Sultanate' shapes of 1241
the Hejaz, whose Ayyubid suzerainty the Rasulids ended in 1238 when Nur al-Din Umar captured Mecca

correction.text: 1241-1249: Egypt and the Syrian principalities (Cliopatria's mislabelled 'Mamluk Sultanate' 1241 shape), without the Hejaz, which left Ayyubid suzerainty in 1238

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's shape holds only Egypt and the Hejaz (1.23 M km2) and gives the Syrian lands to a 'Mamluk Sultanate' row for 1241-1249 (287,000 km2 in Syria, Jordan and south-east Turkey), but the Mamluk sultanate was founded in 1250. The Ayyubid page: by 1250 an-Nasir Yusuf 'took Damascus with relative ease' and held Syria from the Khabur to Sinai apart from Hama and Transjordan; Jerusalem was regained in 1244-45. The corrected shape is the union of the two Cliopatria rows. fx-27: the Hejaz is subtracted. The Ayyubid page: "The Rasulids later ended Ayyubid suzerainty in the Hejaz, which they completed in 1238 when Nur al-Din Umar captured Mecca"; ledger event 1238 (vassal_end, region Hejaz) already says so, and the unsubtracted shape put 651 Hejaz cells in dispute with the Sharifate of Mecca in 1241.

correction.text: Syria from the Khabur to Sinai, ruled from Aleppo, without Hama and Transjordan

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1250-1260: the Syrian rump under an-Nasir Yusuf, who 'ruled from Aleppo' and controlled 'Syria from the Khabur River to the Sinai Peninsula, apart from Hama and Transjordan' until the Mongols took Aleppo in 1260. Cliopatria draws these years as Mamluk (its 1250-1259 Mamluk shape includes Syria). Egypt went to the Mamluks in April 1250, confirmed by the treaty of April 1253.

region.text: Egypt, 'effectively taking control of the country'

ledger.note: 1171: Saladin ends the Fatimid caliphate and founds the Ayyubid state in Egypt. Infobox 'Established by Saladin: 1171'; 'In 1171, al-Adid died and Saladin took advantage of this power vacuum, effectively taking control of the country'.

region.text: Cyrenaica (Barqa), the coast of eastern Libya that the Ayyubid shape covers

ledger.note: 1172-1173: Cyrenaica taken for Saladin. The page says of the conquests outside Egypt: "He captured Siwa in 1172 and conquered Cyrenaica before 1174." The page does not name who held Cyrenaica; placed in 1173, the last year before the 1174 keyframe (added by fx-27).

region.text: the Hejaz and the sharifate of Mecca

ledger.note: 1174: the Hejaz comes under Saladin. The page says he sent Turan-Shah in 1173 'to conquer Yemen and the Hejaz'; no event dates the Hejaz itself. Around 1200 Qatada ibn Idris 'seized power in Mecca and was recognized as its emir by al-Adil', i.e. the sharifs ruled under Ayyubid suzerainty.

region.text: Zabid (May 1174) and Aden (later in 1174)

ledger.counterpart: Zabid, Aden and Sanaa (the three previous independent states; rulers not named on the page)
ledger.note: 1174: Turan-Shah takes Zabid and Aden for Saladin. 'In May 1174, Turan-Shah conquered Zabid and later that year captured Aden.' The page names no previous rulers of the two; Cliopatria's 'Mahdids' row is Omani and is not this state.

region.text: Damascus, welcomed by the governor on 23 November

ledger.note: 1174: Saladin enters Damascus. After Nur al-Din's death in 1174 he was 'proclaimed as the first Sultan of Egypt'; 'on November 23 he was welcomed in Damascus by the governor of the city'.

region.text: Hama and Homs with their citadels

ledger.note: 1175: Hama and Homs fall to Saladin. 'By mid-1175, Saladin had conquered Hama and Homs.' Homs was handed to the descendants of Shirkuh in 1179 (Ayyubid page).

region.text: Sanaa, from the Hamdanid rulers

ledger.counterpart: Hamdanids of Sanaa (Yemen; not the Cliopatria 'Hamdanid Emirates' row)
ledger.note: 1175: Sanaa taken. Turan-Shah 'took Sanaa in 1175', driving out its Hamdanid rulers.

region.text: most of Hadramawt

ledger.note: 1180: Hadramawt conquered. 'The Ayyubid deputy Uthman al-Zandjili conquered most of it in 1180.'

region.text: Edessa, Saruj, Raqqa, Qirqesiya, Nusaybin, Sinjar and Amid

ledger.note: 1182: the Jazira falls. 'First, Edessa fell, followed by Saruj, then Raqqa, Qirqesiya and Nusaybin'; Sinjar 'fell after a 15-day siege on 30 December'; the Saladin page places the capture of Amid in 1183. Raqqa, Sinjar and Nusaybin were given back to Imad al-Din Zangi II as Ayyubid vassal territories (Ayyubid page). The page headings give 1182-83; the individual sentences carry no year.

region.text: Aleppo and its territory

ledger.note: 1182: Saladin takes Aleppo. 'In May 1182, Saladin captured Aleppo after a brief siege'; 'Aleppo formally entered Ayyubid hands on 12 June' (the page gives no year for the second sentence; the Saladin page: 'By 1182, Saladin had completed the conquest of Syria after capturing Aleppo').

region.text: the Zengid lands of Mosul, left in Zengid hands in March 1186

ledger.note: 1186: Mosul bound to Saladin by treaty. 'Upon Abbasid encouragement, Saladin and Mas'ud negotiated a treaty in March 1186 that left the Zengids in control of Mosul'; the Zengids gave up the territory east of the Lesser Zab to Ayyubid authority and agreed to provide military aid when asked.

region.text: the Kingdom of Jerusalem's land, Hattin to Jerusalem

ledger.note: 1187: Saladin destroys the crusader army at Hattin (4 July). 'In this battle alone the Crusader force was largely annihilated'; Gaza was captured in 1187.

region.text: Jerusalem and Gaza, with the Frankish hinterland taken after Hattin

ledger.note: 1187: Jerusalem capitulates on 2 October. 'Jerusalem capitulated to his forces on Friday, 2 October 1187'; he 'captured Gaza in 1187'; 'Saladin had captured almost every Crusader city' (Tyre held out).

region.text: the coast from Tyre to Jaffa, 'essentially a coastal strip'

ledger.note: 1192: the Franks keep the coast. At Ramla (1 or 2 September) 'the Christians would hold the coast from Tyre to Jaffa'; 'Jerusalem would remain under Islamic control' and Ascalon's fortifications were to be demolished and the town returned to Saladin.

region.text: the Kingdom of Jerusalem's land, Hattin to Jerusalem

ledger.note: 1192: the Treaty of Ramla ends the fighting for the Holy Land. 'It was signed on 1 or 2 September 1192' and 'guaranteed a three-year truce between the two armies'.

region.text: the Zengid lands of Mosul, Cliopatria's 1202 Zengid shape

ledger.note: 1202: Mosul's Zengids stand apart again. Page silent on when the 1186 arrangement ended; Cliopatria's Zengid row reappears in 1202 on the land its Ayyubid 1192 shape had swallowed. Al-Adil was recognised as sultan by the Abbasids only in 1207.

region.text: Yemen under Nur ad-Din Umar

ledger.note: 1229: Yemen declares itself independent. 'Following Mas'ud ibn Kamil's death in 1229, Nur ad-Din Umar declared his independence' and stopped paying the annual tribute. The Rasulid page's infobox says 'Established 1229' but its text says he 'proclaimed himself ruler in his own right in 1235'; Cliopatria draws the Rasulids from 1236.

region.text: Jerusalem with a narrow corridor to the coast, Bethlehem, Nazareth, part of Sidon, Jaffa and Toron; the Muslims kept the Temple Mount

ledger.note: 1229: al-Kamil surrenders Jerusalem to Frederick II. 'The treaty was concluded on 18 February 1229, and also involved a ten-year truce'; 'al-Kamil surrendered Jerusalem with the exception of some Muslim holy sites', and Frederick 'also received Bethlehem and Nazareth, part of Sidon district, and Jaffa and Toron'.

region.text: the Hejaz and Mecca, captured by Nur al-Din Umar

ledger.note: 1238: the Rasulids end Ayyubid suzerainty in the Hejaz. 'The Rasulids later ended Ayyubid suzerainty in the Hejaz, which they completed in 1238 when Nur al-Din Umar captured Mecca.' The Rasulid page says they 'temporarily held control over the holy city' and that the Mamluks later 'increase[d] their influence in Hijaz'; no page opened dates the return, so the Hejaz is a gap after 1238.

region.text: Jerusalem, regained by as-Salih Ayyub

ledger.note: 1244: al-Salih Ayyub regains Jerusalem. The page says that after the victory at Hirbiya (La Forbie) 'he gained possession of Jerusalem' (1244-1245); the page is silent on a Khwarazmian role.
1250: the Ayyubid seat moves to Aleppo, where an-Nasir Yusuf rules the Syrian rump. Infobox: 'Aleppo (1250-1260)'.

region.text: all of Egypt, held by the Mamluks under the April 1253 treaty

ledger.note: 1250: the Bahri Mamluks seize Egypt. 'The Bahri Mamluks revolted against the sultan and killed him in April 1250'; 'In April 1253, a treaty was signed whereby the Mamluks would retain control over all of Egypt' and 'Ayyubid rule was officially ended in Egypt'. The Mamluk page puts the murder of Turanshah on 2 May 1250.

region.text: Syria, the Ayyubids' remaining territories

ledger.note: 1260: the Mongols destroy the last Ayyubid state. 'In 1260, the Mongols sacked Aleppo and conquered the Ayyubids' remaining territories soon after.' Homs followed to Baibars in 1262, Kerak c. 1263 and Hama in 1341 (Mamluk dossier).

wars.name: Saladin's conquest of Syria and the Jazira
wars.outcome: Saladin took Damascus (1174), Hama and Homs (1175), Aleppo (1182) and the Jazira cities (1182-83); Mosul stayed Zengid by the March 1186 treaty.
wars.note: The Saladin page dates Hama/Homs to 1175, Aleppo to 1182 and Sinjar to 30 December; Mosul was never taken.

wars.name: Battle of Hattin and the Ayyubid conquest of the Kingdom of Jerusalem
wars.outcome: Hattin (4 July 1187) destroyed the crusader army; Jerusalem capitulated on 2 October 1187; Tyre held out.

wars.name: Third Crusade

zones.text: the coast from Tyre to Jaffa

wars.outcome: Richard took Acre; the Treaty of Ramla (1/2 September 1192) left the Franks the coast from Tyre to Jaffa and Saladin Jerusalem, with a three-year truce.
wars.note: The crusade's own page was not opened; 1191 is the first year the pages date (Ascalon dismantled 1191, Acre taken by Richard); the crusade began earlier.

wars.name: Sixth Crusade

zones.text: Jerusalem with a corridor to the coast

wars.outcome: By the treaty of 18 February 1229 al-Kamil ceded Jerusalem (not the Temple Mount), Bethlehem, Nazareth, part of Sidon, Jaffa and Toron for a ten-year truce; Frederick entered Jerusalem on 17 March 1229.
wars.note: Only the treaty year is read; the crusade's earlier campaign was not.

wars.name: Rasulid independence and the loss of Yemen and Mecca
wars.outcome: Nur ad-Din Umar declared independence in 1229 and stopped the tribute; the Rasulids ended Ayyubid suzerainty in the Hejaz by capturing Mecca in 1238.
wars.note: The Rasulid page's text dates independence to 1235; its infobox says 1229.

wars.name: Fall of the Ayyubids in Egypt
wars.outcome: The Bahri Mamluks killed the sultan in April 1250 and the April 1253 treaty left them all of Egypt.

wars.name: Mongol conquest of Syria
wars.outcome: The Mongols sacked Aleppo in 1260 and conquered the Ayyubids' remaining territories soon after; the Mamluks took Syria after Ain Jalut.

certainty.note: No survey lines: Arabian, Jazira and Nubian frontiers are approximate. The coast from Tyre to Jaffa is sharp from the Treaty of Ramla (1192), and the 1229 Jaffa treaty's Jerusalem corridor is a described line, but neither is a surveyed border.

notes:
Cliopatria rows to correct: (1) the row ends in 1249 but the page ends the dynasty in 1260; (2) its 1241 shape holds only Egypt and the Hejaz and the Syrian principalities sit in the 'Mamluk Sultanate' row for 1241-1249 (the mamluk-sultanate dossier marks that shape wrong); the Mamluk 1250-1259 shape includes Syria, which was Ayyubid until 1260 (new keyframe ayyubid-sultanate_1250); (3) the 1192-1201 shape swallows Cliopatria's Zengid shape (Mosul): the page shows a vassal, not direct land; (4) Jerusalem and its corridor are drawn through 1229-1243 although Frederick II held them; (5) Yemen leaves the Ayyubid shape in 1236 but the pages put independence in 1229 (Ayyubid page, Rasulid infobox) or 1235 (Rasulid text); (6) the Hejaz stays in Cliopatria through 1249 though the Rasulids took Mecca in 1238 and held it 'temporarily'.
Not settled: who ruled Zabid and Aden before 1174 (the page names only the Hamdanids of Sanaa); the date of Aleppo's capture is 1182 on the page as read, other accounts differ and the page's 'on 12 June' carries no year; when Mosul's vassalage ended (vassal_end at 1202 is confidence 1); the return of the Hejaz after 1238; the Ayyubid principalities of Hama (to 1341), Homs (annexed 1262) and Kerak (c. 1263) outlived the 1260 end and are in the Mamluk ledger; the Fifth Crusade and the 1240s wars between Ayyubid branches were not read (page budget).
Counterparts that need dossiers: the Yemeni states of Zabid, Aden and Sanaa (1170s); the Sharifate of Mecca; the Ayyubid principalities of Hama, Homs and Kerak. The page's 'Nominal vassal of the Abbasid Caliphate' (Cliopatria relation 1202-1249) is not coded as an event: the Abbasid dossier should carry it.
